A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching main results and readable Appendices A–I. However, v1 contains Figure D.3's caption without its chart, limiting comparison of the CIFAR-10 numerical results and comparator membership.

before.justification: Appendix D reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including empirical bound comparisons, weight spectra, and sensitivity to width and Schatten indices.

after.justification: Appendix D retains these original experiments and additionally displays the CIFAR-10 comparison chart in Figure D.3.

M1.justification: The Schatten-based analysis, parametric interpolation, loss-function augmentation, and extensions to linear, fully connected, and convolutional networks remain unchanged. No training or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate fully connected networks on MNIST and convolutional networks on CIFAR-10. The newly visible Figure D.3 concerns the CIFAR-10 experiment already described in v1.

E2.justification: Figure D.1 retains Bartlett, Golowich, Neyshabur, Long–Sedghi, Pinto, and Graf comparisons; Figure D.6 retains Graf. Because v1 lacks Figure D.3's chart, its precise comparator membership cannot be checked against v3. The added related-work citations do not establish additional empirical baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains the MNIST widths 300, 400, 500, and 700, weight-decay selection and margin criterion, and CIFAR-10 widths 100–1000, spectral regularization, and margin procedure. No experimental protocol change is stated.

E4.justification: The spectral-decay analyses, layerwise optimized Schatten indices, fixed-index width sweeps, and comparisons with and without loss augmentation are retained. Displaying Figure D.3 supplies a benchmark comparison rather than a new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify one trained network per CIFAR-10 architecture. Neither adds repeated-run information, seeds, empirical error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 supplies plotted CIFAR-10 bound values in Figure D.3, where v1 provides only a caption and qualitative discussion. The other experimental plots retain their values and trends, including the 0.2793 reference test error. This is additional quantitative reporting, not evidence of improved performance between versions.

T1.justification: Equations C.11 and C.12 gain explicit sqrt(L) factors, accompanied by an explanation of logarithmic depth dependence. The main theorems and proofs remain unchanged. New footnote 6 also introduces a full-rank width-scaling expression inconsistent with the adjacent paragraph.

C1.justification: V3 removes the introduction's claim that dependence on norms and margin that is neither linear nor purely logarithmic is unique in the literature. The central claims about rank-sensitive Schatten bounds and interpolation between norm-based and parameter-counting behavior remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 removes the explanation attributing an extra sqrt(L) factor at p=0 to uniformity over Schatten indices. New discussion explains depth factors arising from logarithms of products of norms. The limitations concerning weight versus activation rank and vacuous large-network bounds remain.

D1.justification: The disclosed architectures, regularization settings, margin selection, and hardware—128 CPUs, 500 GB RAM, and DGX A100—are unchanged. No new implementation instructions or code/data access information are supplied.

R1.justification: V3 adds works on PAC-Bayes derandomization, nearly tight VC dimensions, and rank-sensitive bounds by Li et al. Section 2 revises its account of Biggs and Guedj, while Appendix C.4 adds a comparison involving network Jacobians and unit spectral norms.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in related work, Sections 3.2–3.3, and the conclusion, plus updated acknowledgements and bibliography text and removal of the brief impact statement. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain.

P2.justification: V3 includes the previously absent Figure D.3 chart and re-renders the experimental graphics. Figure D.4 moves to the next page and surrounding text reflows. The remaining figure structures and comparison tables are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the previously missing CIFAR-10 comparison inspectable and improves the qualifications and depth-factor accounting in comparisons with prior work. These are limited gains because the main theory and experimental design remain unchanged. A new width-scaling inconsistency in footnote 6 slightly offsets the improved clarity.
